claim: Ohio Revised Code Section 3107.07(K) violates the 14th Amendment to the United States Constitution by arbitrarily denying equal protection and the due process right to be heard at a meaningful time and in a meaningful manner on a petition for adoption, but Ohio Revised Code Section 3107.11(B) does not independently violate the constitutional right to due process because, notwithstanding its confusing and misleading language, the notice provision is sufficiently accurate to satisfy constitutional requirements.
initial_reasoning: In 2019 Ohio 5380, the court held that §3107.07(K) violated the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment but did not find it violated the Equal Protection Clause. The court also held that §3107.11(B) did not independently violate due process, agreeing that the notice provision was sufficiently accurate. Thus the claim incorrectly asserts an equal‑protection violation and misstates the court’s findings.
